title: Inversion
summary: Place a negative or restrictive adverb at the start of a sentence and invert subject and auxiliary.

theory.markdown:
**Inversion** means placing the auxiliary verb **before** the subject. It is used for emphasis in formal or literary English.

**When to use inversion:**
After negative or restrictive adverbial expressions at the start of a sentence:

- **Never, rarely, seldom, hardly, scarcely**: *Never have I seen such a mess.*
- **Not only ... but also**: *Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.*
- **Only then / Only when / Only after**: *Only then did I understand.*
- **No sooner ... than**: *No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang.*
- **Hardly/Scarcely ... when**: *Hardly had I left when it started to rain.*
- **Under no circumstances / On no account**: *Under no circumstances should you sign that document.*
- **So + adj**: *So tired was she that she fell asleep immediately.*

theory.title: Inversion triggers and patterns
rows: Not only does it look bad...
I had hardly sat down when...
Hardly had I sat down when...

items.source: Rarely do we get such perfect weather.
items.translation: Rzadko zdarzaja nam sie takie idealne warunki pogodowe.

items.source: Not only did he forget my birthday, but he also forgot our anniversary.
items.translation: Nie tylko zapomnial o moich urodzinach, ale tez o naszej rocznicy.

items.source: Under no circumstances should you give them your password.
items.translation: W zadnym wypadku nie powinienes dawac im hasla.

exercises.source: I have never heard such beautiful music.
answers: Never have I heard such beautiful music.

exercises.prompt: Not only ___ (did/does) she speak French, but she also speaks Japanese.
exercises.hint: Present fact -> does; inversion needed after 'Not only'.

exercises.prompt: Hardly ___ I got home when the storm started.
exercises.explanation: 'Hardly ... when' -> Past Perfect inversion: Hardly had + subject + past participle.

exercises.sentence: Only then I realised my mistake.
answers: Only then did I realise my mistake.
exercises.explanation: 'Only then' triggers inversion: only then + auxiliary (did) + subject.

exercises.source: W zadnym wypadku nie powinienes o tym mowic.
answers: Under no circumstances should you talk about this.
On no account should you talk about this.

exercises.source: She rarely admits when she is wrong.
answers: Rarely does she admit when she is wrong.
Rarely does she admit she is wrong.

exercises.prompt: No sooner ___ she spoken than everyone started to applaud.
exercises.hint: No sooner + had + subject + past participle + than.

exercises.prompt: Only after the meeting ___ we learn the full story.

exercises.sentence: Not only he was late, but he also forgot his report.
answers: Not only was he late, but he also forgot his report.
exercises.explanation: 'Not only' at the start triggers inversion: Not only + auxiliary + subject.

exercises.source: Nigdy wczesniej nie widzialem tak wiele gwiazd.
answers: Never before had I seen so many stars.
Never had I seen so many stars before.

exercises.prompt: So ___ the soup that nobody could eat it.
exercises.explanation: So + adjective at start triggers inversion: so salty was it that...

exercises.prompt: Scarcely ___ (had/have) we left when the fire alarm went off.
Build an inverted sentence with 'Not only'.

exercises.source: Zaledwie usiadlem, gdy telefon zaczal dzwonic.
answers: Hardly had I sat down when the phone started ringing.
No sooner had I sat down than the phone started ringing.
